question: Can an AI coach get you to a sub-3 marathon?
title: Can an AI coach get you to a sub-3 marathon? One runner is testing it
description: Not proven yet. I'm testing it on myself: five AI coaches plan my training for a sub-3 marathon at Chicago on October 10, 2027. Here are my real Garmin numbers, updated every month.
answer: Not proven yet. I'm testing it on myself. Five AI coaches plan my running, lifting, food and recovery for a sub-3 marathon at the Chicago Marathon on October 10, 2027, and I publish the numbers as they come in.
On {start_date_long}, my Garmin predicted a {start_marathon} marathon. On {now_date_long}, it said {now_marathon}. I need 2:59:59.

sections.h2: Where I am, from my Garmin
paras: Threshold pace is roughly the fastest pace I can hold for an hour, measured by my Garmin with a chest strap. I've been faster than I am today, which is part of why I think the gap can close.

Kai, the running coach, builds every week from a published marathon training method and my Garmin data. The plan climbs from about {week_plan_miles} miles a week now to a peak near 90 in September 2027, with hill sprints every week.

Rook, the head coach, settles it when the running, strength and nutrition coaches want different things. Anything I report, like pain, comes first. Then the race. Every change is written down with the rule behind it.

sections.h2: How you'll know if it worked
paras: The test has checkpoints: a 5K on February 6, 2027, a 10K on May 15, a half marathon on September 5, then Chicago. Each result goes on this site with the official time. If the AI coaching falls short, that goes on here too.

question: Is there an AI coach for running and lifting together?
title: AI coach for running and lifting together: how mine keeps them from colliding
description: My AI coaching team plans running and strength training together. The head coach decides when they clash, so heavy leg work never lands the day before a hard run.
answer: Yes. Mine is a team: Kai plans the runs, Bo plans four short lifts a week, and Rook, the head coach, decides when they clash. The main rule: heavy leg work goes after the hard runs, never the day before one.
I'm using it to train for a sub-3 marathon at Chicago on October 10, 2027, and this is how my week actually looks.

sections.h2: My week, running and lifting together
table: Heavy lower body, after the run
Speed lower body, after the run
No legs: the long run is next
paras: Each lift is short, about 40 to 45 minutes, and always after that day's run.

sections.h2: How the coaches settle a clash
paras: Bo, the strength coach, wants my legs strong. Kai, the running coach, wants them fresh for the hard days. When they disagree, Rook decides in the same order every time: anything I report, like pain, first. Then the marathon. Then my weight. Then strength. So the run usually wins.
Lower-body days sit on the same days as the hard runs, after the run, so the legs get a full day or more before the next hard effort. Saturday stays free of leg work before the Sunday long run.
Right now it coaches one runner: me. If it gets me to Chicago, the people on the waitlist get to try it first. It isn't medical advice, and the coaches are AI characters.

question: Is there an AI running coach for heavier runners?
title: AI running coach for heavier runners: what mine watches for a 258 lb start
description: I started training for a sub-3 marathon at 258 lb. Here is what my AI running coaches watch for me: easy effort by heart rate, daily foot checks, and steady eating.
answer: I started this at 258 lb, chasing a sub-3 marathon at Chicago in October 2027. My AI coaches don't treat that as a reason to go easy on the goal. They watch three things closely: how hard my easy runs really are, how my feet feel each morning, and whether I'm eating enough to run.
This is one heavier runner's setup, not medical advice.

table: A heart-rate range learned from my own easy runs (109 to 120 bpm right now)
Pace alone would push me too hard on easy days
A 0 to 10 check each morning, first steps out of bed
Pain I report is the one signal that changes a run that day
No more than about 2 lb a week, eating to hunger
Logged for miles, left out of my pace readings
Pushing my son in the jogging stroller makes pace meaningless

sections.h2: What hasn't changed because of my weight
paras: The goal. The plan still builds to sub-3 marathon training: hill sprints every week, fast pickups, long runs, and a peak near 90 miles a week in September 2027. The numbers on this site show whether that works.
